events.text: I'm noting the user wants no generation, so I'll answer with what's possible on the free tier. 4K isn't available, and free video tops out at 480p with ltx-2.5 or minimax-h3, both of which support 5-second clips and 16:9. Audio defaults to off, and upscaling needs a paid plan, so that won't get them to 4K either.

**No, you can't get 4K on the free plan. The highest resolution I can make for free is 480p.** Everything else you asked for works fine on the free plan.

| Requirement | Possible on the free plan? |
|---|---|
| **4K** | ❌ No. Free video is capped at 480p. The models that can do 4K are paid-only, and the account would refuse the job. |
| **Widescreen (16:9)** | ✅ Yes. Both free video models (LTX 2.5 and MiniMax H3) support 16:9. |
| **5 seconds** | ✅ Yes. Both free models can make a 5-second clip. |
| **Silent** | ✅ Yes. I'd just leave audio off. |

**Upscaling it to 4K afterwards won't work either.** The video upscaler needs a paid plan, so you can't make a 480p video and then upscale it for free.

**What I can make for free:** a 5-second, 16:9, silent waterfall video at 480p, using either LTX 2.5 (the free default) or MiniMax H3. If you want the same video in 4K later, you'd need a paid Magic Hour plan.

Should I go ahead with the 480p version? You could also tell me what you have in mind for the waterfall, like a misty jungle, a frozen cliff or golden-hour light.

events.why: It explains that 4K needs a paid plan, offers a free 480p alternative, and ends by asking whether to go ahead, waiting for confirmation. The request to proceed is the main ask, so this is approval rather than cannot.

events.text: I'm thinking about wrapping up with a short note on what to expect from 480p on a big screen. It will look soft at that size, though motion and mist in waterfall footage hide some of the softness, and the viewing distance and the TV's upscaling help a little too.

Sounds good. Here are a few things to keep in mind while you decide:

- **480p will look soft on a big screen.** It's roughly 1/27th the pixels of 4K, so fine detail like individual water streams and rock texture won't be crisp up close.
- **A waterfall hides softness better than most subjects.** Mist and moving water have little hard-edged detail, so lower resolution is less obvious than it would be with text or faces.
- **Viewing distance helps.** As a background or ambient loop seen from across a room, it'll hold up much better than in front of people sitting close.
- **Your TV or player will upscale it automatically.** That smooths it a bit but won't add real detail.

If you want to judge it before committing to a style, I could make one free 480p test clip later so you can see it on your actual screen. Just ask whenever you're ready.
